channel.title: Otago Daily Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Otago Daily Times (odt.co.nz)

item.title: Crime 'entitled' Bunnings to snag shoppers' facial data
item.description: Bunnings used CCTV to scan the faces of customers entering 63 stores over three years. Photo: Getty Images Bunnings is within its rights to use facial recognition software on customers in Australia to curb theft and violence against staff, with a tribunal laying the foundation for a broader rollout.

item.title: Elderly woman targeted for money: police
item.description: A woman is before the courts accused of stealing more than $5000 from elderly women living alone in Hamilton and Auckland.

item.title: Rates cap plan ‘problematic’
item.description: Cutting costs to align with local government reforms is like using a rusty pocket knife to perform surgery, an Invercargill city councillor says.

item.title: Summer Sounds Music Festival heading to Bluff
item.description: Darcy Kerr performs at last year’s Summer Sounds Bluff. PHOTO: SUPPLIED Bluff’s popular annual Summer Sounds concert will take place from 2pm on Sunday, February 15 at the Bluff Oyster Festival site in Barrow St.

item.title: Harold still a high point for students
item.description: Life Education Trust Southland teacher Teresa Wallace and Harold the giraffe have been working together for 19 years teaching children about health and wellbeing. PHOTO: SUPPLIED Children and teachers are back at school and so are Harold the giraffe and his sidekick Teresa Wallace.

item.title: Sharing skills on how to snap shots
item.description: As mobile capability and technology have developed, so have the skills of the Invercargill Photography Club members. PHOTO: SUPPLIED Smartphones have opened up an uncharted landscape for the next generation of shutterbugs, a photographic society executive says.

item.title: New sign language class child-tailored
item.description: Every Sign tutor and interpreter Jaime Randhawa uses speech and sign language to communicate with her baby daughter Rubie. PHOTO: NINA TAPU Sign language classes especially designed for tamariki will start in the Deep South next week.

item.title: Boat ramp partial refund possible
item.description: Annual Bluff boat ramp subscriptions users may be receiving a surprise partial refund or subscription extension.

item.title: Food insecurity rising; support requests up
item.description: Hayz@theAnchorage owner Haylee-Chanel Simeon (left) takes a delivery of vegetables from Kiwiharvest relationship manager Jennifer Stephens. Ms Simeon is one of the Kiwiharvest volunteers who makes meals for kaumātua in Bluff. PHOTO: SUPPLIED The demand for food parcels and meals climb as food prices continue to rise, support agencies say.

item.title: Record year for deer processing charity
item.description: Mighty Meats butcher Cory Orlowski has once again been voluntarily processing tonnes of venison into the small hours of the morning for Deer to Care. PHOTO: TONI MCDONALD Deer to Care has doubled down on its commitment to donate tonnes of wild venison and pork to community organisations in need.
